WORKSHEET · CLASS 25 · AGES 4 YEARS

Build a Shape Spaceship Worksheet for Age 4

A rocket with four shape-shaped holes: match the pieces, color the parts, and the spaceship is ready to fly.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This worksheet turns the spaceship game into paper practice: your child matches shapes to the holes they fit, then colors each part. Matching a shape to a shaped hole is the same skill as recognizing a letter shape later — the eyes learn to compare outlines.

  • Matching shapes to shaped spaces
  • Naming circle, triangle, square and rectangle
  • Coloring with some care inside big regions
  • Talking through a plan before starting

On the sheet: Match each shape piece to the rocket hole it fits, then color the rocket.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class behind it.

This worksheet belongs to Shapes, Patterns & Sorting (Class 25) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole shapes collection lives at /worksheets/shapes/. One finished sheet is a full session — download it, print it, and let the fridge door be the gallery.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 25 · AGES 4 YEARS

Silly Monster Factory Worksheet for Age 4

A friendly monster with empty spots for eyes, horns, arms and feet — design him on paper with shapes.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The monster game is open-ended building, and the worksheet keeps that spirit: your child draws shape parts onto the monster, inventing as they go. There is no wrong monster, which makes this a favorite for children who avoid “wrong answers”.

  • Drawing circles, triangles and rectangles on purpose
  • Counting parts as they are added (how many eyes?)
  • Making creative choices and describing them
  • Fine motor control for small shapes

On the sheet: Draw shape eyes, horns, arms and feet on the monster — then invent a monster friend of your own.

The class behind it.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 25 · AGES 4 YEARS

Hot Air Balloon Patterns Worksheet for Age 4

AB and AAB patterns to finish with a pencil: say the pattern out loud, then draw what lands next.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Patterns are the first real maths rhythm. On paper your child reads the row left to right, says the pattern like a little song, and draws or colors the missing shape. The game plays the same way on screen — the sheet just slows it down and adds pencil control.

  • Reading a row left to right
  • Hearing and continuing AB and AAB patterns
  • Predicting what comes next and committing to it
  • Drawing small shapes with growing control

On the sheet: Finish each pattern row: draw or color the shape that comes next.

The class behind it.

Candy Shape Shop Worksheet for Age 4

Sort the shop’s candy by shape: circle candies here, square candies there — with scissors practice built in.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Sorting by shape means your child has to decide, not just copy: each candy card gets one look, one decision, one box. Cutting the cards first adds scissor practice — a two-skills-one-sheet deal.

  • Sorting by one clear rule (shape)
  • Scissor control along a dotted line
  • Saying the sorting rule out loud
  • Checking a sorted pile for mistakes

On the sheet: Cut out the candy cards and glue each one in the right shape box.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 25 · AGES 4 YEARS

Rainbow Window Puzzle Worksheet for Age 4

The rainbow windows lost their glass: match each shape to its dashed outline and the light comes back.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This sheet asks your child to match solid shapes to their outlines — the exact mechanic of the window game. Outline matching is harder than it looks: the eyes must ignore color and size and read pure shape.

  • Matching solid shapes to outlines
  • Ignoring color to find the shape
  • Careful line drawing between columns
  • Shape vocabulary: naming each match

On the sheet: Draw a line from each shape to its matching outline.

What your child practices.

This sheet carries the wizard’s full spell: three pattern rows that grow from two-shape AB patterns to three-shape ABC patterns. Your child reads, says, and draws the next shape — the ABC row is a genuine step up in working memory.

  • Holding three items in mind (the ABC row)

  • Precision drawing of small shapes

Peacock Feather Symmetry Worksheet for Age 4

The peacock’s left feathers are missing: finish the mirror picture so both sides match.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Symmetry is a matching game against yourself. Your child completes the left side of the peacock so it mirrors the drawn right side — eyes comparing two halves, pencil copying curves in reverse. It is challenging and deeply satisfying.

  • Understanding mirror symmetry
  • Copying curves in reverse
  • Checking both halves against the mirror line
  • Careful coloring to make both sides match

On the sheet: Finish the left side of the peacock so both sides match, then color them the same.

The class behind it.

Shape Detective Mystery Worksheet for Age 4

A scene full of mixed shapes: find them, circle them, count them — the detective’s case, on paper.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The detective game asks children to find shapes hiding inside objects; the sheet gives a busy scene of mixed shapes to search, circle and count. Searching, circling and counting in one task is a genuine three-step workout — and the count makes your child check their own work.

  • Visual search among distractors
  • Circling with control
  • Counting a set after finding it
  • Recording a number in a box

On the sheet: Find and circle the shapes, then count each kind and write the number.
